text: Testing plays a key role in software development. Unit tests check small parts of code, like individual functions, while integration tests make sure different parts work together correctly. Many developers use test-driven development, or TDD, which means writing tests before writing the actual code. This approach helps catch problems early and keeps the code clean. Although writing tests takes extra time, it gives programmers real confidence. When tests pass, developers know their changes did not break anything. As a result, teams can update software faster and with less fear. In short, good testing saves time and leads to more reliable products.
